div.head: Duns 1
div.ab: Hoc est: si uestigium furati pecoris minetur de loco in locum, tunc committatur ipsum uestigium landhominibus uel cum marca monstretur, quod rectum prosequantur.
Ðæt is: gif man trode bedrifð forstolenes yrfes of stæðe on oðer, ðonne befæste man þæt spo[r] landesmannum oððe mid mearce gecyðe, þæt man riht drife.

That is, if a man follows up the track of stolen cattle from one bank to the other [across the river], then he [shall] entrust that trail to the local people or prove with evidence that he is making a legal pursuit.

Nämlich: (Von der Spur gestohlenen Viehes. lq) Wenn jemand die Fährte gestohlenen Viehes von einem [Wye-?]Ufer ans andere leitet, dann übergebe er diesen Spurfaden [dort] heimischen Leuten, beziehungsweise [falls er ihn jenseits verlor] erweise durch Merkmal, dass er Rechtliches verfolge.

Namely: (Of the track of stolen cattle. lq) If anyone follows the track of stolen cattle from one [Wye?] bank to the other, then let him hand over that trail to the people of the land [there], or [if he lost it on the far side] show by a mark that he is pursuing [it] lawfully.
div.note: B reads ‘spon’; Liebermann supplies ‘spor’ from Ld. The rubrics marked ‘lq’ come from the lost exemplar of Ld and the Quadripartitus and are not original. Liebermann compares VI As 8.4.
